question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil, SIA, is reviewing the annual disclosure calendar for Pragati Foundation, a NPO registered on NSE-SSE. Under Regulation 91(C) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations 2015, by when must the NPO make its annual disclosures on financial aspects?

answer.text: Within 30 days from the end of the financial year.
Within 60 days from the end of the financial year.
Within 180 days from the end of the financial year along with the audited Form 10B.
By October 31st of each year OR before the income-tax return due date, whichever is later.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Regulation 91(C)(i) of LODR expressly provides that financial-aspect disclosures by a NPO listed or registered on SSE must be filed by October 31st of each year or before the due date of filing the income-tax return under the Income-tax Act 1961, whichever is LATER (non-financial aspects follow the 60-day rule). **The Trap:** 60 days is the deadline for NON-financial annual disclosures (91(C)(ii)); 30 days and 180 days are not deadlines specified under 91(C). Form 10B is an income-tax audit report, not a SSE filing. **Cross-Exam Context:** III-A/III-C Compliance tests 91(C) deadlines for SSE-listed entities; V-A sees Form 10B on the 80G donor-side. XXIII requires the SIA to cross-map LODR disclosure dates to Annual Impact Report signing windows. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Build a single Gantt for each NPO engagement with three columns: 60-day non-financial bucket, October-31/ITR financial bucket, and the AIR bucket under 91E. Missing the financial-disclosure date is a SEBI-Act penalty matter, not a cure-by-letter matter.
